text:
The son was an intended donee beneficiary, but his rights never vested because he learned of the contract only after the owner and the landscaper had already changed the payee and the owner had paid the landscaper. Until a beneficiary assents, sues, or relies, the original parties may discharge or modify the promise, so the son has no claim. The plaintiff will most likely not prevail; the answer is C.

CONFIDENCE: 90
